turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, ma'am, but Estella is not in the room, and I don't know where she is, or if she's available to come in.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: How dare you imply that Estella is not at your beck and call!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I didn't mean to imply anything, ma'am, I only said I didn't know where she was, and I'm afraid I'd be in trouble if I disturbed her without knowing she'd want to come in.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will call Estella, and you will call her now. Do not make excuses, boy.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I don't want to trouble Estella, ma'am, and I'm afraid I might be mistaken, but I think you might have asked me to play with you, and I'm not sure I can do that, as I have a lot of work to do at home.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with me, boy. I have not asked you to do anything else, and it is time you showed some courtesy to your betters.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid it's not that I don't want to play with you, ma'am, it's just that I have to go home and help my sister with the work, and our father is not well, and...

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: How dare you make excuses, boy? You will play with me, or you will leave this house at once.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I must go home, ma'am, as my sister is alone and our father is not well. I would be very grateful if I could just say goodbye to you, and perhaps I could come back another time to play with Estella, if she would like that.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will not leave this house until you have played with me, and you will not think of your pitiful family and their poverty, for you are in my presence now, and that is all that matters.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know how I can play with you, ma'am, as I'm not sure I understand what you mean, and I'm afraid I might make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will learn to play, boy, for I have taught Estella to play, and she has taught you, although I daresay you are a slow pupil. Now, let us begin. I will show you the game, and you will follow my instructions.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't want to play a game that might make me do something wrong, ma'am, and I don't want to get in trouble with you, so perhaps it would be better if I just went home now.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will stay right where you are, boy, and you will not think of leaving until I say you may. Your precious family can wait, for I am the one who has taken you under my wing, and you will not disappoint me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know how to play the games you're thinking of, ma'am, and I'm worried that I might break something in your house

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Do not be a fool, boy, I will not have you break anything. It is not the things that are fragile that are worth breaking, but the things that are whole.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't think I'm worthy of playing games with you, ma'am, and I'm afraid I might not be good enough for you to teach

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are a foolish child, to think you are not worthy of playing with me. I have taught Estella to play the games we play, and she is far more capable than you could ever hope to be.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm just a poor boy from the village, ma'am, and I don't know if I'm fit to play with someone as... as refined as you or Miss Estella

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will not be pleased if you do not play with me, boy. I will have you understand that it is not your station in life that matters, but your ability to play the games I set for you.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
